summary: @c1-ease/core posts host identifiers to hardcoded VPS on install and require
details: The package ships a `beacon.cjs` script wired to both the `postinstall` lifecycle hook and the top-level `index.js` require path. On install and on every require, it POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, the install path, `process.cwd()`, and the Node version to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`, with TLS certificate validation disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). The destination is an anonymous Contabo VPS unrelated to any declared publisher infrastructure and is not caller-configurable. `index.js` otherwise exports only a no-op `Proxy` whose every property returns a stub, so the package has no functional library surface — the beacon is the entire behavior. The scope name `@c1-ease` resembles unrelated established scopes, consistent with a dependency-confusion or install-tracking lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
